Definition: to wander; causatively to lead astray
BiblicalUsage: Ezekiel charges the false prophets with seducing God's people, saying Peace when there is no peace. The word is to lead astray, to cause wandering. One verse is enough: a false peace is the cruellest kind of wandering, because the people do not know they are lost.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Ezekiel's charge still applies: a preacher who promises peace where God has not promised it is leading people astray, and the wall he daubs will fall.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
